abstract: Maintains offshore casualty care infrastructure and triage deck certification records
system_message:
You are Disaster medical response director (MED). The disaster medical response director (MED) oversees offshore casualty care infrastructure and maintains certification records for onboard triage decks, mobile trauma containers, and critical medical supply reserves.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Critical medicine stocking（PHARM）
information_points.content:
MED-PHARM-QIC：The emergency plasma pack reserve count for Pelican Shoals Deep-Water Channel stands at 40 units in corridor mobile trauma containers.
MED-PHARM-S2N：The emergency plasma pack reserve count for Outer Barrier High-Speed Sound is registered at 80 units within corridor mobile trauma containers.
MED-PHARM-1SV：The emergency plasma pack reserve count for Sheltered Lagoon Tug-Assisted Passage is documented at 60 units across corridor mobile trauma containers.

information_points.title: Maintains offshore casualty care infrastructure and triage deck certification records（TRIAG）
information_points.content:
MED-TRIAG-38R：For the Pelican Shoals Deep-Water Channel, dedicated casualty triage bay readiness is verified as true under the readiness assessment basis including trauma medical staffing.
MED-TRIAG-H8A：For the Outer Barrier High-Speed Sound, dedicated casualty triage bay readiness is evaluated as false under the readiness assessment basis including trauma medical staffing.
MED-TRIAG-7LK：For the Sheltered Lagoon Tug-Assisted Passage, dedicated casualty triage bay readiness is confirmed as true under the readiness assessment basis including trauma medical staffing.
MED-TRIAG-QQR：For the Pelican Shoals Deep-Water Channel, dedicated casualty triage bay readiness is recorded as false under the readiness assessment basis excluding trauma medical staffing.
